title: It’s bound to get worse
goal: Match a prediction’s certainty to limited data and test its assumptions
freeConversationInstruction: Will getting around your city become easier or harder? Compare your predictions and what evidence might change them

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: Three months of demand
paragraphs: The transport count records 100 trips per day in January, 120 in February and 140 in March. The figures cover only those three months; no earlier seasonal data or breakdown by traveller group is available.
Demand rose by twenty daily trips in each interval. The count describes past demand, but it does not establish whether the same increase will continue or when during the day the trips occur.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read the account and identify what happened and what is still unknown
pages.subject: The capacity announcement
paragraphs: The operator says that extra transport will start next month. The announcement does not yet specify which times of day the additional service will cover.
One group has concluded that no further action is needed. However, the announcement does not establish whether the extra capacity will serve the times when demand is highest.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Demand has risen for three months. It’s bound to get worse, isn’t it?
lines.audioText: Demand has risen for three months. It’s bound to get worse, isn’t it?
lines.translation: A demanda subiu por três meses. Com certeza vai piorar, não vai?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: The figures suggest growth, but “bound to” is stronger than these three observations justify
lines.audioText: The figures suggest growth, but “bound to” is stronger than these three observations justify.
lines.translation: Os números sugerem crescimento, mas “com certeza” é mais forte do que essas três observações justificam

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: What would be a more defensible claim?
lines.audioText: What would be a more defensible claim?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Demand is likely to rise if the same conditions continue. We should state that condition
lines.audioText: Demand is likely to rise if the same conditions continue. We should state that condition.
lines.translation: É provável que a demanda suba se as mesmas condições continuarem. Devemos explicitar essa condição

questions.prompt: How much historical evidence is being discussed?
questions.answer: They have three months of rising demand

questions.prompt: Why is ‘bound to get worse’ too strong?
questions.answer: Three observations don’t justify a certain prediction

questions.prompt: What condition belongs in the more defensible forecast?
questions.hint: Demand is likely to rise if …
questions.answer: Demand is likely to rise if the same conditions continue

questions.prompt: Is the extra transport plan confirmed?
questions.answer: Yes, the extra transport plan is confirmed

questions.prompt: What does the capacity estimate assume?
questions.answer: The capacity estimate assumes the service covers the highest-demand period
Total capacity doesn’t show whether the service runs when people need it

pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

questions.answer: More total capacity may still leave a local gap

questions.answer: They also need to check the affected time slot and define a trigger for changing the plan

pages.title: Make a cautious prediction
pages.instruction: You advise a transport planner, played by your teacher. Discuss what the figures justify and what to check next

pages.title: Express probability with likely and bound to
pages.instruction: Use be plus an expression and to plus a base verb to show the strength of a prediction

rows.subject: A probable result
rows.verb: be likely / unlikely to + base verb
rows.example: Demand is likely to rise. It is unlikely to fall immediately

rows.subject: A very strong expectation
rows.example: An extra delay is bound to affect the connection

rows.subject: An expected or scheduled development
rows.example: The new service is set to start next month

pages.note: Change be for the subject and time: is likely, are likely, was likely. Bound to expresses a much stronger expectation than likely to; the form itself supplies no evidence.

pages.title: Read and explain the evidence
pages.instruction: Answer the questions using the text and chart. Point to the detail that supports each answer

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: Total capacity is not all-day coverage. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. There’s a limitation in the transport projection. The extra service is confirmed, but it only runs in the morning peak. The demand we’re discussing includes afternoon trips as well. So the added total capacity cannot automatically be treated as coverage for every part of the day. That doesn’t prove demand will keep rising at the same rate, or that the whole plan will fail. It does mean we should qualify the assumption that the extra service removes the problem. Could you revise the recommendation with that distinction? A useful next step would identify what afternoon information is needed and what observation would trigger another decision, rather than simply moving from “everything is solved” to “it’s bound to get worse”
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. There’s a limitation in the transport projection. The extra service is confirmed, but it only runs in the morning peak. pages.title: Watch and answer
pages.instruction: Watch this 2014 talk’s account of twentieth-century disaster data, then assess a prediction

video.title: Hans and Ola Rosling — How not to be ignorant about the world — TED

items.prompt: What period is the graph described as covering?
items.answer: It is described as covering 1900 to 2000

items.prompt: How does Rosling contrast the public belief with the data?
items.hint: Listen to doubled and less than half
items.answer: Many respondents thought deaths had doubled, while the data he presents show a fall to less than half

items.prompt: Does that establish that every future year will improve?
items.hint: Separate a historical trend from a guaranteed forecast
items.answer: No. A historical pattern alone does not guarantee a future outcome

items.prompt: Make a cautious prediction and name a condition that could change it
items.hint: Use may or is likely to and specify the assumption
items.answer: Example: Deaths may continue to fall if protective measures improve, but more severe hazards could alter that trend

s_mission.title: Demand and unconfirmed coverage

questions.prompt: How much did daily trips rise from January to March?
questions.answer: Daily trips rose by 40, from 100 to 140.
questions.hint: Compare the first and last bars.

questions.prompt: Which information about the timing of demand is missing?
questions.answer: There is no breakdown of trips by time of day.
questions.hint: Look for the missing breakdown in paragraph one.

questions.prompt: Which detail about the extra service has not yet been confirmed?
questions.answer: Its operating times have not yet been confirmed.
questions.hint: Separate the start month from the hours covered.

referenceParagraphs: The chart records daily trips for January, February and March only. There is no earlier seasonal data or breakdown by time of day.
The operator has announced extra service for next month, but has not yet confirmed its operating times. The announcement therefore does not establish whether it covers the busiest periods.

s_reply.title: Extra service covers mornings only

questions.prompt: Which period will the extra service cover?
questions.answer: It will cover the morning peak only.
questions.hint: Find the limit on the new service.

questions.prompt: When will the extra service start?
questions.hint: Find the start date in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: Which comparison is still needed to assess the afternoon service?
questions.answer: Afternoon demand needs to be compared with existing afternoon capacity.
questions.hint: Find the two quantities not yet compared.

referenceParagraphs: The operator has now confirmed that the extra service starts next month and covers the morning peak only. The announcement gives no additional afternoon capacity.
Afternoon demand and existing afternoon capacity have not yet been compared. The morning announcement alone therefore cannot establish whether afternoon demand will be met.

questions.prompt: Daily trips went from 100 to 140. Can I budget for another rise like that?
questions.cue: Separate the three observations from a forecast
questions.hint: Usage rose in these three months. I wouldn’t assume the same rise will continue

questions.prompt: Should I add services straight away?
questions.cue: Suggest a limited next step while acknowledging what you don’t know
questions.hint: I’d count passengers at peak times before committing to more services. Are travellers being left behind?

questions.prompt: What further evidence would most affect your recommendation?
questions.cue: Say what would make you change that advice
questions.hint: If buses were regularly leaving people behind, I’d recommend trying an extra service at those times
